subject: Renewal: Geo-handshake — EU edge migration + APAC warm-tier coordination
messages:
From: Asha Menon <asha.menon@panasia.health>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Berger <tberger@euroclinic.co.uk>
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Renewal kickoff — EU residency transition + APAC rollout questions

Hi Jasmine and Marissa,

Thanks for the renewed conversation around our upcoming contract. As we start the renewal discussion for PanAsia Health Systems, two technical/legal constraints are top of mind from our governance and privacy teams:

- We need the EU region to be the primary processing and storage region for all EU patient traffic (data-in-rest and processing).
- We plan to open APAC in phases for new customers in Q1–Q2 2027; we want a staged rollout where production traffic originates in APAC but fails back to EU edge nodes in the event of regional outage.

Specifically, before we sign: can Redwood commit to an EU-edge primary tenancy migration (we will need data migration and acceptance criteria) and an APAC staged-burst plan with a warm-tier cross-region fallback?

I've attached a draft SOW and a short requirements spreadsheet with our expected steady-state QPS and monthly token estimate. For procurement, Tom is looping in the contract team.

High-level timeline we are targeting: procurement & legal sign-off by mid-November, phased APAC pilot in Jan 2027, full APAC availability by Apr 2027. Can you confirm feasibility and outline the next technical/deployment steps?

Thanks,
Asha
Director, Cloud Platform & Compliance
PanAsia Health Systems

Attachments: PAN-Health_SOW-draft-20261010.pdf, requirements-eu-edge-apac-staging.xlsx
From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Menon <asha.menon@panasia.health>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 12:08:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Renewal kickoff — EU residency transition + APAC rollout questions

Hi Asha —

Really appreciate the clear requirements. Short answer: yes, we can support moving PanAsia's EU traffic to EU-edge as the primary tenancy and run an APAC staged rollout with a warm-tier failover, but there are a few items we need to align on up-front.

Immediate asks from our side so we can produce a detailed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and timeline:

1) Confirm expected steady-state and peak tokens / second (you gave monthly estimates; can you provide 95th percentile RPS for the busiest hour?)
2) Is PanAsia willing to use customer-managed KMS for EU keys (required for EU-held-encryption in some jurisdictions)? If yes, we will need KMS details and an initial key material exchange window.
3) Network: will you provide a dedicated IP range for peering, or do you prefer IP allowlists per environment? Peering windows will determine the migration blackout windows.
4) Acceptance criteria: suggested acceptance tests: (a) no data exfiltration outside EU in the EU-primary path, (b) per-route latency SLOs in EU-edge <= 120ms 95th, (c) successful failover & failback test with <90s control-plane handoff.

We can set a 60–90 day technical runway once contracts and SOW are finalized. I'll loop in Karthik to put together a pricing sketch for Dedicated + Warm-tier failover.

Would you and Tom be available for a 45-minute technical kickoff next Tue (Oct 12) 09:00 SGT / Mon Oct 11 21:00 UTC? If that time doesn't work, propose alternatives.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Sr. Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: preliminary-MAP-template.docx (sent internally; will share on kickoff)
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Menon <asha.menon@panasia.health>, jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 08:46:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Renewal kickoff — pricing and slotting options

Hi Asha —

Great to see the timeline. From a commercial perspective we can offer two routes that map to the technical options Jasmine called out:

Option A — EU-Primary Dedicated (Recommended for residency):
- Reserved Dedicated pool in EU-edge nodes (monthly commitment).
- Includes isolated tenancy, customer-managed KMS support, and higher retention for audit logs.
- Pricing: baseline commit + per-token overage. (See attached pricing sheet for sample tiers.)

Option B — Hybrid Dedicated + Warm-tier (Recommended for staged APAC rollout):
- EU-edge Dedicated for EU traffic; APAC uses Redwood Hosted with a Warm-tier reserved capacity that can be promoted to Dedicated on short notice.
- Cross-region warm standby (control-plane orchestrated failover) can be included as an add-on; recommended warm-up windows during business hours for stateful KVs.
- Pricing: separate APAC warm reservation (lower commit) + failover activation fee.

I attached a draft pricing workbook with ballpark numbers based on the monthly token estimate you shared. If you can provide 95th percentile RPS (Jasmine's point), we will refine the commit tiers and breakpoints.

Next steps I propose: 1) confirm technical open questions in the kickoff, 2) we deliver a MAP + SOW redline within 3 business days, 3) procurement signatures and initial invoice by Nov 15 to meet your target.

Attachments: pricing-options-dedicated-warmtier.xlsx

- Marissa
VP, Commercial (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 14:15:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Renewal kickoff — draft runbook and timeline

Hi Asha / team —

Following our quick kickoff this morning (thanks all), I put together a draft runbook that maps the migration and APAC staging into three workstreams: Data Migration + Validation, Network/Peering & Security, and Ops/DR Testing.

High-level schedule (draft):
- Week 0–2: Finalize SOW + sign contract / KMS exchanges.
- Week 3–6: EU-edge tenant provisioning; config drift checks; pre-cutover data snapshot and encryption key validation.
- Week 7: Dry-run failover test (control-plane only) into APAC warm-tier. Capture logs and run acceptance checks.
- Week 8–10: Cutover window — migrate EU production routes to EU-edge (planned maintenance window, 2–4 hours). Post-cutover validation and telemetry baseline.
- Week 11–14: Gradual APAC seeding (pilot customers) with warm-tier monitoring; week 12 run a full failover test (stateful) and validate RPO/RTO targets.

Dependencies and open items:
- IP ranges for peering and firewall windows (PanAsia to confirm).
- Compliance evidence: SOC2 report and encryption attestation required by PanAsia legal (we can provide SOC2 report and our KMS integration guide).
- SLA exceptions: if you require a <60s failover for certain flows, that will require additional dedicated control-plane redundancy; we'll need to price that.

Acceptance criteria we will use for the EU-edge migration:
1) All EU-routed requests show EU-edge processing and storage in audit traces for 30 minutes post-cutover.
2) No EU-origin data appears in non-EU regions for 7 days after migration.
3) Failover tests complete within the agreed control-plane window and meet latency/throughput targets.

I'll attach the runbook draft and a checklist; happy to iterate. If PanAsia can share the final RPS figures and procurement contact details, Marissa can get DocuSign ready.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Team —

Thanks for the updates and the call notes. We're aligned on the overall approach but procurement/legal have a few asks before we can move to signatures:

1) Please provide a formal Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with 90-day milestone commitments and named owners for each task.
2) We submitted SOW redlines (attached) — please review the data residency clause language (section 4.2) and confirm the exact sentence you will accept to ensure EU-primary residency is contractually enforceable.
3) Can you provide a short list of test dates for the dry-run and full failover (Mon–Fri windows) between Oct 25 and Nov 12? We need them to book our privacy & ops teams.

If you can turn around the MAP and an updated SOW by end of next week (Oct 22 EOD UTC), we can keep to PanAsia's mid-November signature target.

Regards,
Tom Berger
